items.claim: The scene-turn digit holds only under an unstated verse-initial restriction, both pointed runs labeled byte tier re-collate at NFD only, and the in-span paseq segment is dropped while five parashah marks are cited.
items.evidence: Re-collation of the row's two pointed runs against their own cited verses returns nfd, not byte — בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֔וּא against MT 19:16 and יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ שְׁלִ֣ישִׁיָּ֔ה לְמִצְרַ֖יִם וּלְאַשּׁ֑וּר against MT 19:24 — so the '(byte tier)' label on each is false and both need re-splicing from source bytes rather than re-keying. The counted object is under-specified: the consonantal skeleton of the day-formula stands in SIX verses of the row's own span (sweep: MT 19:16, 19:18, 19:19, 19:21, 19:23, 19:24 — 6 verses, skeleton tier), not five. The digit is recoverable only if the swept object is silently narrowed to verse-initial onsets, which drops the mid-verse instance בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֑וּא inside MT 19:21 — the class-vs-occurrence blend the count discipline exists to bar, and the row names no such restriction. The same skeleton also runs well past the row's close — MT 20:6, 22:8, 22:12, 22:20, 22:25, 23:15, 24:21 (sweep: 13 verses across chs 19-24) — so it cannot carry the weight of bounding this passage, only of structuring inside it. Disclosure is asymmetric within one span: five setumah citations are correct against the mark inventory at MT 19:15, 19:17, 19:18, 19:23, 19:25 (single-witness, tier-3, never a driver), while the paseq segment recorded at MT 19:16 (1 seg, single-witness, count-only) goes unmentioned inside the very span those marks are swept over. The contrast drawn against earlier sub-units closed by a postpositive divine-speech signature carries no quoted form and no verse anchor; the postpositive sites actually available to it are MT 17:3, 17:6 and 19:4 (sweep: 3 verses in chs 17-19), and a device claim with no quoted form is insufficient engagement. No ketiv/qere note falls anywhere in 19:16-25, so the slicing here is otherwise safe.

items.claim: The 'no internal tier-1 seam' warrant is argued past its strongest counterevidence: a verse-initial divine-speech onset at MT 20:3 coincides with the row's only in-span parashah mark, and both pointed runs labeled byte tier re-collate at NFD only.
items.evidence: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר יְהוָ֔ה opens MT 20:3 verse-initially. That adjacency class is a tier-1 divine-speech frame in the frame policy, not a narrative aside (sweep: 52 verses book-wide carry the amar/vayomer-plus-YHWH adjacency, MT keys), and the single setumah inside this span — MT 20:2, single-witness, tier-3 — falls at exactly that junction. The row discloses the mark as falling 'mid-span' but never sets it against the frame onset it abuts, so the assertion that the bytes offer no internal seam between command and interpretation is stated rather than tested. The tier-3 layer cannot drive a cut and is not asked to here; the point is that the tier-1 onset it corroborates is left unengaged. The frame at MT 20:2 is also mislabeled: בָּעֵ֣ת הַהִ֗יא דִּבֶּ֣ר יְהוָה֮ בְּיַ֣ד יְשַׁעְיָ֣הוּ introduces the COMMAND, whose imperative run follows in the same verse as לֵ֗ךְ וּפִתַּחְתָּ֤ הַשַּׂק֙; the interpretation of the sign-act is what opens under the MT 20:3 onset. Calling 20:2 the interpretive frame inverts the two. Both pointed runs re-collate at nfd, not byte, against their cited verses, so the '(byte tier)' labels are false. Credited: the servant handling is right and is exactly the distinction this book demands — עַבְדִּ֥י יְשַׁעְיָ֖הוּ at MT 20:3 is one of the three named referents (sweep: 23 verses carry the my-servant form book-wide), correctly kept apart from the unnamed-figure zones, and the row decides no referent question. The disclosed deviation from the report label toward third-person narration is likewise honestly carried rather than argued away.

items.claim: The sentence that defeats the row's own rival is falsified by the row's own quoted bytes — MT 21:6 carries a divine-speech frame with an explicit addressee, and the span's petuchah stands immediately before it.
items.evidence: כִּ֣י כֹ֥ה אָמַ֛ר אֵלַ֖י אֲדֹנָ֑י at MT 21:6 is both a frame-device and an addressee marker: אֵלַ֖י is an explicit first-person dative inside the formula. The rejected-alternative warrant that the banquet-to-commissioning transition 'is not marked by an addressee or frame-device shift in the bytes' therefore cannot stand as written — the row quotes the disqualifying run two sentences earlier in its own rationale, so the rival it concedes is left undefeated. The corroborating layer points the same way: the mark at MT 21:5 is a petuchah, the rarer type (41 PE against 168 SAMEKH over 209 marked verses; single-witness, tier-3, never a driver), and it sits at the 21:5|21:6 junction. Ten verses later the same formula class is treated as a tier-1 boundary driver at MT 21:16, so opposite weights are applied to one frame class inside one chapter without an argument reconciling them. Credited, and it is the harder half to get right: frame ownership at MT 21:6 is correctly named as the divine frame even though the title stands behind an intervening dative — a non-adjacent title form that a formula-adjacency reading would misclassify as unowned. Disclosure is asymmetric: paseq segments are recorded inside this span at MT 21:2 (2 segs) and MT 21:8 (1 seg), single-witness and count-only, and neither is mentioned while both parashah marks are. Both pointed runs re-collate at nfd, not byte, against MT 21:1 and MT 21:6. The header itself is verse-initial and correctly claimed, and the fold disclosure for the header verse is accurate and properly held at tier-4.

items.claim: The bounds are byte-clean and survive challenge, but both pointed runs labeled byte tier re-collate at NFD only and the 'bracket' reading overstates an intra-verse doubling whose two members differ in the bytes.
items.evidence: The seams are not contested and the byte evidence supports them: verse-initial massa headers stand on both sides, מַשָּׂ֖א דּוּמָ֑ה opening MT 21:11 and the next header opening MT 21:13, with setumah marks at MT 21:10 and MT 21:12 (single-witness, tier-3, corroboration only). No paseq segment and no ketiv/qere note falls in 21:11-12, so nothing is owed there. Nor does any byte-true device straddle either seam: the watch vocabulary of the preceding unit is a DIFFERENT root — הַֽמְצַפֶּ֔ה at MT 21:6 and מִ֨שְׁמַרְתִּ֔י at MT 21:8 — from the watchman noun here, so the continuity is thematic and in the English, not a shared form in the Hebrew, and the header cut is clean. Two defects remain. Both pointed runs re-collate at nfd rather than byte against MT 21:11, so the '(byte tier)' labels are false and the runs need re-splicing. And the doubled question is called the verse's 'own bracket' although it is an immediate intra-verse repetition, not an inclusio around the unit, and its two members are not the same form — שֹׁמֵר֙ מַה מִלַּ֔יְלָה שֹׁמֵ֖ר מַה מִלֵּֽיל pairs a full and a shortened night-form. That is a recurrence claim carrying no tier label; at skeleton tier the two members still differ, so no tier makes them identical.

items.claim: An undisclosed catchword hooks this row's closing verse to the next unit's at an oracle join, the mark prose places a setumah inside a span it does not fall in, and the in-span paseq is dropped at the very verse whose setumah is cited.
items.evidence: קֶ֣שֶׁת stands in the row's last verse MT 21:15 and recurs at MT 21:17 as מִסְפַּר קֶ֛שֶׁת — skeleton tier, the accents differ (sweep: that noun at MT 21:15, 21:17, 22:3 across chs 20-23, 3 verses). That is a catchword hook straddling the row's own closing seam at an oracle join, and it is the byte support for precisely the rival the row concedes and then dismisses — keeping the Arabia material whole. Undisclosed, it argues continuity against the cut; the cure is disclosure and a warrant that survives it, not silence. The mark prose states that a setumah opens this row at MT 21:12, but MT 21:12 lies outside the span 21:13-15 and that mark closes the preceding verse; the mark is real and correctly typed, its position relative to the span is not. In the same span the paseq segment recorded at MT 21:15 (1 seg, single-witness, count-only) is undisclosed although that same verse is cited for its setumah — one verse carrying two disclosure layers, one engaged and one dropped, which is the sharpest asymmetry in this cluster. items.claim: The parallel drawn to the earlier frame is false at every tier — the two openings differ in token order — and it collapses the adjacent/non-adjacent title distinction on which the earlier site's classification rests.
items.evidence: MT 21:6 reads כִּ֣י כֹ֥ה אָמַ֛ר אֵלַ֖י אֲדֹנָ֑י and MT 21:16 reads כִּי כֹ֛ה אָמַ֥ר אֲדֹנָ֖י אֵלָ֑י: the dative precedes the title at the first site and follows it at the second. The two therefore fail identity at skeleton tier as well as at byte, and 'identical frame construction' is asserted with no tier label at all — a recurrence claim of the kind that must be tier-labeled at write time. The difference is not cosmetic. The earlier site is the non-adjacent title form, and it is exactly that form which the divine-frame classification has to ARGUE rather than read off an adjacency; the later site is the plain adjacent form that needs no such argument. Flattening the two into one construction erases the ground on which the earlier frame was owned, and it is the one distinction a frame-ownership claim in this chapter cannot afford to lose. Both frames are divine, which the row gets right, and naming the speaker class rather than a bare count is correct practice. Credited: the remnant object is named correctly — וּשְׁאָ֧ר מִסְפַּר קֶ֛שֶׁת גִּבּוֹרֵ֥י at MT 21:17 is the noun, kept apart from the name and from the reactivating clauses (sweep: the vav-prefixed form stands in 8 verses book-wide, the bare noun in 12). The bare unpointed mention of the root beside it is skeleton grade and is not labeled as such. Both pointed runs re-collate at nfd, not byte, against MT 21:16 and MT 21:17. The undisclosed catchword tying MT 21:15 to MT 21:17 across this row's opening seam is charged to the neighbouring unit but bears here too.

items.claim: The stated discriminator for the closing seam is byte-false: the in-that-day frame the row says is absent from its own span stands inside it at MT 22:8.
items.evidence: MT 22:8 reads וַיְגַ֕ל אֵ֖ת מָסַ֣ךְ יְהוּדָ֑ה וַתַּבֵּט֙ בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֔וּא אֶל נֶ֖שֶׁק בֵּ֥ית הַיָּֽעַר. The run בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֑וּא, quoted by the row from MT 22:12, collates against MT 22:8's bytes at accent_stripped tier and is skeleton-identical there — the two differ only in the accent borne by the second token. The row's claim that the in-that-day frame is 'not present anywhere in this row's own span' is therefore falsified by a verse inside that span, and it is the claim on which the seam is argued. No positional reading rescues the contrast either: the formula is verse-initial at NEITHER site — at MT 22:8 it follows the verb of looking, at MT 22:12 it follows the divine subject — so an onset-versus-adjunct restriction, which the row does not make, would not separate them. Worse for the warrant, the device runs THROUGH the seam and beyond it (sweep: skeleton at MT 22:8, 22:12, 22:20, 22:25 — 4 verses in ch 22), so it is cross-seam cohesion evidence arguing continuity, the opposite of the discriminating force claimed for it, and it is not disclosed as such. What actually survives at 22:11|22:12 is the change of subject the row also states — וַיִּקְרָ֗א אֲדֹנָ֧י יְהוִ֛ה צְבָא֖וֹת introduces a new grammatical subject not present in 22:1-11 — and the seam may well hold on that ground alone; the defect is that the load-bearing sentence as written is contradicted by the row's own span. Credited, and it is a real contrast with the rest of this cluster: every pointed run here reaches BYTE tier on re-collation. The mark handling is type-correct, the absence of any parashah mark in 22:1-11 is correctly left unclaimed rather than treated as counterevidence, the paseq counts at MT 22:2 and MT 22:11 (1 seg each) are right, the verse-initial header claim is right, and the poetry-line observation is accurate and correctly held at tier-4 (0 across all eleven verses in the staged layout). One further defect: those paseq segments are cited under a WEB prefix, though that seg layer exists only in the Masoretic witness and is keyed to it — the chapter is identity-numbered so the digits land, but the witness attribution does not.

items.claim: The closing formula is not a bracket in the bytes — a byte-identical divine-speech run straddles the row's own closing seam into MT 22:15 — and the title recurrence is claimed without its tier.
items.evidence: אָמַ֛ר אֲדֹנָ֥י יְהוִ֖ה collates at BYTE tier against both MT 22:14, where the row places its closing bracket, and MT 22:15, where the next unit opens as כֹּ֥ה אָמַ֛ר אֲדֹנָ֥י יְהוִ֖ה צְבָא֑וֹת. The run the row treats as unit-closing immediately re-opens as the following unit's frame, which argues a repeated frame element rather than an inclusio, and it is undisclosed. The asymmetry is internal to this cluster: the neighbouring unit disclosed the mirror-image recurrence of the same stacked title across THIS row's opening seam and reasoned about it; the closing seam gets no such treatment, and it is the stronger of the two cases because the shared run reaches byte tier rather than skeleton. The bracket claim also carries no tier: אֲדֹנָ֧י יְהוִ֛ה צְבָא֖וֹת at MT 22:12 and אֲדֹנָ֥י יְהוִ֖ה צְבָאֽוֹת at MT 22:14 re-collate against each other at skeleton tier only — the accents differ on all three tokens — so 'the same stacked divine title' is a skeleton-tier recurrence stated as if unqualified, where campaign practice requires the tier named at write time. Credited: every pointed run in this row reaches byte tier on re-collation; the petuchah type at MT 22:14 is correct and not conflated with setumah; the paseq count at MT 22:13 is correct at 2 segs and is correctly presented as a bare count without an intra-verse position, which is the only sourceable form of that claim. One further defect, shared with the neighbouring unit: the petuchah and the paseq are both cited under a WEB prefix although each seg layer is keyed to the Masoretic witness alone.
